entries.name: OCR (Image to Text)
entries.description: Extract text from an image via OCR. Supply a publicly reachable image URL; returns the extracted text plus a confidence score. x402node runs Tesseract; strale runs Claude vision (better on handwriting/photos). Same operation via two gateways.

url.description: Publicly reachable image URL to run OCR on
Echo of the input image URL

text.description: The transcribed text extracted from the image

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/image/ocr?url=<IMAGE_URL>&lang=eng (x402 v1 paid, ~$0.01 USDC on Base). Input is via query params, NOT a JSON body. For the strale gateway: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/image-to-text?image_url=<IMAGE_URL> (or ?base64=<B64>), ~$0.054 USDC on Base.
usage.outputShape: x402node: body.text (string), body.confidence (number 0-100), body.lang, body.lines_count, body.words_count, body.processing_ms, body.file_size_bytes. strale: body.text, body.text_type, body.confidence (string), body.language_detected.
quirks: BOTH backends are GET-with-query-params. Registry recorded strale as POST but its own 402 outputSchema declares GET queryParams (base64|image_url) — POST/JSON-body is wrong for both.
x402node: method is GET; POST returns 404 'Cannot POST /image/ocr'. Image supplied via ?url= query param (publicly reachable image URL).
x402node uses x402 v1 (no top-level accepts array) — agentcash fetch CANNOT pay it ('parse_payment_required'/'x402 v1 not supported'). Pay via qa-pay or a raw x402 v1 client.
x402node lines_count and words_count came back 0 even though text was extracted — rely on body.text and body.confidence, NOT the count fields.
x402node optional ?lang= (default eng); supports eng, chi, jpn, kor, deu, fra, spa, ita.
strale takes EITHER ?image_url= or ?base64= (base64-encoded image); confidence is returned as a string and it adds language_detected/text_type fields.
Despite the registry name 'Image & PDF to Text', only image OCR is verified — PDF support is unverified on both gateways.
Orbis backend (orbisapi.com proxy) DROPPED: known charge-then-404 payment trap, do-not-register.
usage.guide: Extract text from an image via OCR. Supply a publicly reachable image URL; returns the extracted text plus a confidence score. x402node runs Tesseract; strale runs Claude vision (better on handwriting/photos). Same operation via two gateways. GET https://api.x402node.dev/image/ocr?url=<IMAGE_URL>&lang=eng (x402 v1 paid, ~$0.01 USDC on Base). Input is via query params, NOT a JSON body. For the strale gateway: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/image-to-text?image_url=<IMAGE_URL> (or ?base64=<B64>), ~$0.054 USDC on Base. Output: x402node: body.text (string), body.confidence (number 0-100), body.lang, body.lines_count, body.words_count, body.processing_ms, body.file_size_bytes. strale: body.text, body.text_type, body.confidence (string), body.language_detected.

entries.name: DocPull
entries.description: Extract a PDF into clean Markdown for downstream LLM/agent use, billed per call via x402 on Base.

usage.outputShape: body.markdown (extracted text as Markdown string); also body.success (bool), body.pageCount (int), body.charCount (int)
quirks: Registry surface says METHOD=GET, but GET https://docpull.ai/extract returns ONLY an API help/info page (not an extraction) and STILL charges $0.001 — do NOT use GET. The real extraction is POST https://docpull.ai/extract with JSON body {"url":"<public_pdf_url>"}.
Pricing is $0.001 USDC PER PAGE, not per call. A 12-page PDF costs ~$0.012. Budget accordingly for large PDFs.
Free pre-flight: GET https://docpull.ai/probe?url=<pdf_url> returns page count + cost estimate with no payment — call it first to size the cost.
url must be a publicly accessible PDF (no auth/login walls).
usage.guide: Call POST https://docpull.ai/extract with JSON body {"url":"<public PDF url>"} and pay via x402 (USDC on Base). Do NOT use GET — GET only returns a help page yet still bills $0.001. Read the result from body.markdown (clean Markdown of the PDF), with body.pageCount and body.charCount as metadata. Pricing is $0.001 per page; optionally hit the free GET /probe?url=<pdf_url> first to get the page count and cost estimate before paying.

entries.name: Reducto Parse
entries.description: OCR and parse a PDF/image/spreadsheet document into structured text chunks. Returns full extracted content with per-block bounding boxes, confidence scores, and chunked text suitable for RAG/embeddings.

usage.outputShape: response_type='parse'; job_id; duration; pdf_url; studio_link; usage.num_pages; usage.credits; usage.credit_breakdown.page; result.type='full'; result.chunks[].content; result.chunks[].embed; result.chunks[].blocks[].type; result.chunks[].blocks[].bbox.{left,top,width,height,page}; result.chunks[].blocks[].content; result.chunks[].blocks[].confidence; result.chunks[].blocks[].granular_confidence.parse_confidence; result.ocr; parse_mode
quirks: Body field is `document_url` (a public URL to the PDF/image/spreadsheet). The gateway maps it to Reducto's native `input` field, so use document_url here NOT input.

Despite returning a job_id, the parse result is delivered INLINE and synchronously in the same 200 response (body.result.chunks[]). Do NOT poll the job_id; there is no separate status/result endpoint.
response_type is 'parse'. To extract structured fields against a schema use the sibling /extract route instead.
Billed per page: body.usage.credits = pages processed (1 credit = 1 page). x402 fee is a flat $0.05 regardless of page count.
Gateway/check_endpoint_schema publishes an EMPTY inputSchema ({}); the real field set is Reducto's, surfaced only via 422 errors or these verified calls.
studio_link points to a Reducto Studio job viewer (browser UI), not a result API.
usage.guide: OCR and parse a PDF/image/spreadsheet document into structured text chunks. Returns full extracted content with per-block bounding boxes, confidence scores, and chunked text suitable for RAG/embeddings. POST https://api.paysponge.com/x402/purchase/svc_d672d90ggvqqygj60/parse with JSON body {document_url} Output: response_type='parse'; job_id; duration; pdf_url; studio_link; usage.num_pages; usage.credits; usage.credit_breakdown.page; result.type='full'; result.chunks[].content; result.chunks[].embed; result.chunks[].blocks[].type; result.chunks[].blocks[].bbox.{left,top,width,height,page}; result.chunks[].blocks[].content; result.chunks[].blocks[].confidence; result.chunks[].blocks[].granular_confidence.parse_confidence; result.ocr; parse_mode

entries.name: Reducto Extract
entries.description: Extract structured fields from a document against a caller-supplied JSON schema. Returns an array of objects matching the schema, populated from the document's content.

usage.outputShape: response_type='extract'; job_id; usage.num_pages; usage.num_fields; usage.credits; usage.extract_mode='extract'; studio_link; result[] (array of objects whose keys match the provided schema, e.g. result[].title); citations
quirks: REQUIRED fields are `document_url` and `schema` (a JSON Schema object describing the fields to extract). `schema` is a TOP-LEVEL field.

FIELD-NAME TRAP: do NOT wrap the schema in `instructions` (Reducto's public docs show instructions.schema, but this paysponge gateway uses ExtractConfigNew and rejects `instructions` as extra_forbidden). Send `schema` at the top level.
Like /parse, the result is returned INLINE/synchronously (result[] in the same 200 response). Do NOT poll the job_id.
result is an ARRAY of objects (result[]) — one object per extracted record — keyed by the schema's properties.
Billing differs from parse: usage.credits counts pages + fields (observed credits:3 for 1 page / 1 field). The x402 fee was still a flat $0.05.
Gateway publishes an empty inputSchema; the true shape was recovered from a 422 (ExtractConfigNew requires `schema`) then confirmed with a 200.
usage.guide: Extract structured fields from a document against a caller-supplied JSON schema. Returns an array of objects matching the schema, populated from the document's content. POST https://api.paysponge.com/x402/purchase/svc_d672d90ggvqqygj60/extract with JSON body {document_url, schema} Output: response_type='extract'; job_id; usage.num_pages; usage.num_fields; usage.credits; usage.extract_mode='extract'; studio_link; result[] (array of objects whose keys match the provided schema, e.g. result[].title); citations
